_note: The five distribution networks the player lays by hand. Each is a set of LINKS (cables, pipes, ducts) between the buildings named in `connects`; a link costs `linkCost` per level it spans (at least one) and may span at most `maxSpanLevels`. HUBS are the buildings that hand the network out to everything within their serviceRadiusLevels (catalog/buildings/*.json): a junction lights the rooms around it, a cistern waters them, a duct fan airs them — but a hub only works when it is linked back to where the network comes from. The graph is read by systems/infrastructure/networkGraph.js; each system settles its own network over it. A network not listed in config infrastructure.enforced is treated as fully laid (every node joined, every hub reaching everywhere) — which is how system tests isolate one network at a time.

networks.name: Power grid
networks.description: Generators feed junctions by cable; each junction lights every room within its reach, up to its capacity. When the generators run short, junctions are served in priority order (1 first) and batteries cover only the junctions they are cabled to.
networks._note: Loss scales with cable run from the generator plus the drop from the junction to the room, so a shallow level fed from a deep generator pays for every level of cable between.

networks.name: Water mains
networks.description: The water's loop, fresh half. Pumps drive it: a pump pushes the reclamation plant's recovered water, and fresh groundwater for what is lost, up the mains to the cisterns; each cistern stores water and supplies every room and resident within its reach — except the cultivation rooms, which take their water only by pipe, from a cistern or from the next room along. A purifier on the mains cleans the reclaimed water that passes through it.
networks._note: Pumping upward costs power proportional to lift height, so water costs more the higher people live.

networks.name: Sewer
networks.description: The water's loop, dirty half. What a cistern's rooms and residents use comes back dirty. Drains carry it downhill only, cistern to cistern, to a reclamation plant — the cultivation rooms, piped for their water, drain by their own drains too; sewage with nowhere to go is dumped where it was made and fouls that level's air.
networks._note: Gravity is the whole design: a drain never carries anything up, so the plant belongs at the bottom.

networks.name: Foul-air ducts
networks.description: The first half of the air's loop. Sucking duct fans draw the foul air off the levels they reach and send it down the foul-air ducts to the scrubbers — through any oxygen garden on the way, which feeds on it and breathes into it. Air only moves when the loop is closed: foul ducts into a scrubber, fresh ducts out of it to a blowing fan.
networks._note: Airflow is settled in systems/airQuality/airflow.js, over this network and fresh-ducts together: the air runs sucker -> foul ducts -> scrubber -> fresh ducts -> blower.

networks.name: Fresh-air ducts
networks.description: The second half of the loop. Out of the scrubbers, cleaned, the air runs along the fresh-air ducts — through any oxygen garden on them, which breathes into it — to the blowing duct fans, which push it out onto the levels they reach. A scrubber or garden the air does not pass works on its own level only.
networks._note: A duct fan may carry both lines. What it does with its own levels is set by suck or blow; air can still pass through it on either line.
